```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.

Answer: This step uses Prokka to predict and identify genes present in the genome bins. It compares predicted protein sequences with databases of known proteins to identify homologous genes and assign possible functions. This helps us understand the potential functions of the microorganisms.
-->

Gene prediction and annotation of the most complete bins with Prokka. Commands for this step were run in `prokka/`.

Change directory to prokka:
```bash
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka
```


Try running prokka for a single bin: observation of steps:
```bash
cat ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```


Next pick a bin to test with. Look at the list of bins you made in step 5: metabat.30

These instructions use metabat.5, substitute id where appropriate:
```bash
bin=metabat.30
prokka --cpus 2 --outdir $bin --prefix $bin  ../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa
```
Note: --cpus 2 option stops prokka from using more than two CPUs
      This command runs on the RStudio server itself, which everyone in the class shares.
      

List contents for metabat.30:
```bash 
ls metabat.30
```


Run prokka on all the metagenomes within a slurm job:
```bash 
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=90
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2 --mem=2gb

echo "Starting prokka in $(pwd) at $(date)"

shopt -s expand_aliases
alias prokka='apptainer run -B /pvol/:/pvol /pvol/data/sif/prokka.sif prokka'

while read bin;do 
  prokka --cpus 2 --outdir $bin --prefix $bin "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa";
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

echo "Finished prokka in $(pwd) at $(date)"
```

Submit job: 
```bash 
sbatch run_prokka.sh
```
